problem:

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{xy+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

examples.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/e79145a13ada389ac337a69f8c48952f53b70d5caf48d950b305275ed8773b44.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/a4de8e3eca77241030facac81ea44493400e00e34d1c7dde9ee9b25eab8441b0.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/5ee75b93739a5018486c6b65a5e5c996f95b7f8ea6fdf6bd68b5727742e770fa.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})=3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/a8fd9120b29337c656c9b715bfa38dbecc7755e50877fad9719de54ed248a8ed.png)

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/445be7536a39ee9c8d90f4cee571bf46acb5c995a9b53547f1aa582bd351592a.png) we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/44faf9caacb8100249410ce233429c030fc52656be35c31d22f423397288da03.png)

The tangent to $f$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
z - f(\mathbf a) = \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $f(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/5824c66708813f59e2920287d35500ea68356ead4a4c3673d8807a0b81ca1abe.png)

feedback.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{yz} \\ {x}^{2}y{z}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} &  \\ 2xy{z}^{2} &  & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{yz})=\frac{1}{yz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2xy{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})={x}^{2}{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{yz} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} & -\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ 2xy{z}^{2} & {x}^{2}{z}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$
